data.title: Power Issue
data.description:
To maintain the sleek and uniform design, Apple provided a power button at the side of the device. This correlation between the power button and the battery is unavoidable for the perfect operation of the iPhone. The iPhone has been designed to maintain it. However, many users have complained about issues regarding issues in their power supply and other power-related errors in their iPhone.

These power issues include:

  • The phone does not turn on.
  • The battery signal doesn’t show on the completely blacked-out phone. Therefore, you cannot determine the problem.
  • iPhone won’t stay charged. The charge drains rapidly after disconnecting from the adapter.
  • The iPhone doesn’t charge. It is stuck on the battery percentage you left it to charge on.
  • Can’t use the iPhone without keeping it on a constant power supply (e.g., connected to a wall adapter or power bank, etc.).

These frustrating problems are, however, the most common issues found on the iPhone XR. There are some widely renowned DIY (do it yourself) fixes available on the internet that may help the issue on your device. Such as

  • Force restart your iPhone (press volume up (+) and quickly press volume down, (-) and then quickly press the power button to complete the restart process).
  • Check your Lightning cable and adapter and see if they are functioning properly.
  • Check if there is any debris on the iPhone XR charging porthole.
  • Limit background processes by stopping the background app refresh.
  • Try charging for 20 minutes while keeping your phone switched off.

Sometimes excessive battery drain can be happening due to a bug that can be resolved by a software update. So try updating your iOS to the latest version. If none of these methods work to resolve the issues on your smartphone, you might need to get it checked by professional technicians. data.description:

Other issues like high ping or latency have often been reported by the users of the phone. The most common reported iPhone XR Wi-Fi issues are…

  • Wi-Fi gets disconnected on iPhone XR.
  • Wi-Fi stays connected, but there is no internet on the receiver.
  • 3. Slow Wi-Fi speeds on metered/non-metered connections on Wi-Fi.
  • High Latency/Ping on Wi-Fi Connections
  • iPhone fails to connect to Wi-Fi.
  • iPhone can’t discover your Wi-Fi connection.

These Wi-Fi issues found on the iPhone XR are pretty common issues found on other wireless-supported devices too! And does not necessarily indicate that there is something specifically wrong with your iPhone XR’s wireless hardware. There are some DIY (do it yourself) fixes available for your smartphone in this case.

  • Check your wireless router. Unplug it from the power source for 10 minutes and try again and see if the issues have been resolved.
  • Turn your Wi-Fi off for five minutes and try again.
  • Forget and reconnect your Wi-Fi connection.
  • Restore the default network connection.

(Reset from here: Settings > General > Reset > Reset Network Connections > *Enter Passcode * > Confirm)

  • Update your iOS to the latest version available.

Signs You Might Need to Replace the Taptic Engine:

  • If your iPhone stops providing vibrations or feedback for notifications, calls, or system interactions.
  • The Taptic Engine works only occasionally or inconsistently.
  • The Taptic Engine produces grinding or buzzing noises that were not present before.
  • Error messages or diagnostics indicate an issue with the Taptic Engine.

Possible Causes of Failure:

  • Physical Damage: Dropping the phone or exposing it to water can damage internal components.
  • Software Bugs: Sometimes, a software issue may mimic hardware failure. Perform a factory reset or update the iPhone before deciding on hardware repair.
  • Wear and Tear: Over time, mechanical components can degrade and stop working properly.

repair_info.image_alt_text: iPhone Xr No Light On Display Issue

data.description:
However, not all damage in display comes from dropping the device from the hands and shattering it. Some users of the iPhone XR have reported a sudden black screen without any prior damage history. The no light on display issue of the iPhone XR is where the user can’t see what’s happening on the phone. The phone runs okay. The phone vibrates, and the user can hear the notification sounds and other inputs. But the problem is they cannot see any of it because the phone display is just plain black. But the phone will respond or might even have incoming calls.

The key symptoms of the “no light on display” issues are

  • The phone display boots up with an Apple logo but doesn’t get past the black screen (iPhone 6–8 Plus).
  • The phone has calls and notifications but doesn’t show anything on display.
  • The iPhone can charge (you can hear the sound that the phone makes while charging) but won’t show anything on the display.

This “no light on display” is usually an internal issue with the LCD connector. However, Apple recommends some processes to practice on your phone to make sure the black screen is not a software glitch.

  • Force Restart your iPhone.

(Press the volume up (+) and volume down, (-) and then press and hold the power button until the Apple logo appears on the screen.)

  • Connect the lightning cable and charge it for 10 minutes. Then try force restarting the iPhone.
  • UNCONVENTIONAL: But press the screen into the phone so it may reconnect any dislodged LCD connector. This fix is not recommended; however, it resolved a lot of the user's black display issues. It might be risky for any layman person.

If none of the fixes work to resolve the issue on your iPhone, you may need to get it looked at by experienced professionals who specialize in iPhone issues. data.title: Ear Speaker Replacement
data.description:
The new iPhone XR offers a new dual speaker setup to Its users. Consisting of one speaker at both the top and the bottom. The top speaker is used for both audio playback and earpiece. The earpiece or the top speaker of the iPhone XR is used the most. Because it is used as both an audio playback speaker and the earpiece of your phone while making phone calls in it. This high level of usage can be a reason to create wear and tear on that speaker very quickly and may cause it to cease functioning properly.

If the earpiece/ ear speaker of your iPhone XR stops working or produces sounds on lower levels you should check some of the factors that might be the reason behind it. Which are:

  • Check if your volume levels are in an optimum range

data.title: Liquid Damage
data.description:
The new iPhone XR is a standard IP68-rated, dust- and water-resistant phone. This means it can resist dust and water coming in up to a certain level. However, it is not completely immune to water getting inside the iPhone and damaging it. Apple has introduced a new technology called LCI. LCI is an abbreviation for liquid contact indicator. Once you have removed the SIM tray, you should see a white/red portion inside the SIM tray region. That is your LCI on the iPhone. If the LCI is completely white or silver, then it is okay. The phone hasn’t contacted any water.

However, if your LCI turns red, you can safely assume that it has been in touch with water and has taken in some water damage.

  • If you have dropped your phone in the water, here are some basic things you should do:
  • Rinse your phone with a lens cloth or a microfiber cloth.
  • You may gently tap the phone with the charger hole against your hand. It may drip the water out if it has gotten in there.
  • NEVER CHARGE YOUR PHONE UNTIL YOU HAVE MADE SURE IT IS COMPLETELY DRY.
  • If anything spills on your phone (like oil, etc.), just rinse the place with a lint-free cloth.

data.title: Face ID Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone xr comes with a distinct feature named Face ID. Where it uses the iPhone user's face to unlock the phone. It also emits an infrared laser to convert your distinct and unique facial features into geometrical and mathematical data for the iPhone.

Face ID is a very complex technology, and users might often misinterpret one of its features as an error in the technology. Here are some common issues regarding the iPhone’s Face ID feature...

  • Face not recognized
  • Face ID is not available at the moment
  • Move the camera a bit lower/higher
  • Upon Unlocking iPhone directly takes me into Passcode and not Face ID.

These common issues however have some home remedies which may work for your iPhone. These fix attempts are risk-free and do not risk damaging your phone.

  • Check if your face ID is on for iPhone Unlock. Go to: Settings > Face ID and Passcode
  • if you use a screen protector make sure it doesn’t obstruct the front camera in any way.
  • Make sure you face the camera and nothing is covering or obstructing between your face and camera region.
  • Restart your phone. Make sure there is no dirt or your front camera lens is not foggy.
  • Update your iOS to the latest version.

If your phone doesn’t unlock with Face ID instead prompts with a passcode. The reasons may be:

  • User might be wearing a face mask while opening the iPhone.
  • The user may have just restarted the device.
  • The phone has not been unlocked in more than 48 hours.
  • The passcode has not been used to unlock the phone in the last 7 days.
  • The device has not been unlocked by face ID in the last 4 hours.
  • The iPhone has a remote lock on and is away from a safe space.
  • If a user fails to unlock the device after five unsuccessful face ID unlock attempts.
  • If at Face ID set up, your iPhone shows or tells you to move the device lower or higher. Chances are that the Device does not support face ID at all.

If your iPhone xr Face ID problems can’t be categorized and sorted by the above-mentioned issues and fixes, you may just need to take it to an extremely diligent iPhone technician to deal with Face ID issues.   • The iPhone has taken on some physical damage. (Dropping from hand)

  • No sound in audio playback
  • No sound in voice calls
  • Distorted sound/low sound on the speakers
  • Headphones not working

  • Phone stuck in headphone mode
  • Ringer switch not working/audio level increases or decreases automatically/physical audio level buttons not working.

These issues are the most common audio issues reported by users in the Apple support forum. There are some “do it yourself” fixes available and advised to be attempted as a “first aid” for your audio issues by Apple professionals and users. Those are

  • Checking the ringer switch to see if it is on the sound mode
  • Restarting Your Phone
  • Disabling your Bluetooth in the iPhone XR
  • Check if your phone is in DND (Do not disturb) mode.
  • Check sound notification settings and try turning noise cancellation off.
  • Try using headphones and check if the sounds come through okay in headphones.
  • Try removing any protective cases.
  • Clean the speaker grills of dirt and debris.

  • The phone gets way too hot while charging and takes a long time to be fully charged.
  • The phone gets hot, and the battery drains drastically.
  • You might see a notification that will say “Temperature high.”
  • The iPhone gets warm on standby mode for no apparent reason whatsoever.

These are some of the most discussed problems in Apple’s user threads and community. However, there are some DIY (do it yourself) fixes that you may try that may help you to resolve your overheating issues.

  • Disable background app refresh.
  • Disable background app refresh from here: Settings > General > Background App Refresh
  • Turn off Bluetooth/location services to reduce processes running in the background.
  • Most of the users have reported they get the heating issue in the latest iOS version. In that case,
  • Try updating your iOS to later versions to check if it works for your phone.
